overview: The two types of sequence found within a eukaryotic gene's primary transcript, one of which is spliced out before translation.
genZNote: Exons make the final cut. Introns end up on the cutting room floor.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A coding region of a gene that is retained in the mature mRNA and translated into protein.
aspects.valueB: A non-coding region of a gene that is transcribed but removed from the pre-mRNA during splicing.

aspects.label: Fate During RNA Splicing
aspects.valueA: Retained and joined together to form the mature, continuous mRNA sequence.
aspects.valueB: Removed by the spliceosome and typically degraded.

aspects.label: Presence in Mature mRNA
aspects.valueA: Present — makes up the final coding (and untranslated) sequence of mRNA.

aspects.label: Occurrence Across Organisms
aspects.valueA: Found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic genes.
aspects.valueB: Common in eukaryotic genes; rare or absent in prokaryotic genes.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: Mutations within exons can directly alter the encoded protein sequence.
aspects.valueB: Mutations at intron-exon splice boundaries can cause aberrant splicing and disease, even though introns themselves are non-coding.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Coding sequence retained in mature mRNA.
